# QRO-Crate 0.1

QRO-Crate is an RO-Crate 1.3 profile for quantum runs, and a checker that holds a crate to it. A crate is accepted or refused by a name and a location, by `python -m qro check`; this page and the files beside it describe the profile to a person and to tools that read RO-Crates.

## Status

- **The IRIs are provisional.** This page is the profile's IRI, and the vocabulary page ([docs/VOCABULARY.md](../docs/VOCABULARY.md)) is its namespace. They are placeholders until a permanent IRI is registered, which changes every crate's identity: no crate is to be published or archived under a provisional one.
- **Version 0.1**, under CC BY 4.0. Its `datePublished`, 2026-10-16, is the day of the build and a placeholder: nothing is published yet, and the date is set when the profile is released.

## The checker is the authority

The shapes below are written for tools that read RO-Crates and cannot run the checker. They never decide a verdict. Each says in its `claims` which refusals of the checker it mirrors, and every must shape adds the six refusals of steps 1 and 2 that can come before its own and that RDF cannot show: `spelling`, `term-unknown`, `graph-form`, `context`, `file-missing` and `file-link`. When a must shape fails, the checker refuses the crate; and when the crate is one fault away from one the checker accepts, it refuses it by one of the names the failing shapes claim. Tests hold that over every plant in this directory, a fuzz, every single edit of the fixture that a pool of 12,591 makes, 469 crates of three families beside it, 124 crates with a key spelt another way, and a walk over any parcel's accepted crate plants (none is built yet). It is not proved, limit 1 says over what, limit 19 says what is held of ids and at which base, and what the shapes do not say is the checker's alone (see the limits below).

## Declaring conformance

A QRO crate's root data entity `conformsTo` exactly Process Run Crate and this profile:

- `https://w3id.org/ro/wfrun/process/0.6`
- `https://github.com/loganw234/QRO-Crate/blob/main/profile/README.md`

and the crate holds a contextual entity for each, as RO-Crate 1.3 requires, exactly:

```json
{
  "@id": "https://github.com/loganw234/QRO-Crate/blob/main/profile/README.md",
  "@type": [
    "CreativeWork",
    "Profile"
  ],
  "name": "QRO-Crate",
  "version": "0.1"
}

{
  "@id": "https://w3id.org/ro/wfrun/process/0.6",
  "@type": [
    "CreativeWork",
    "Profile"
  ],
  "name": "Process Run Crate",
  "version": "0.6"
}

```

A crate that declares another version is refused `context`: this reader reads one version of each profile. The crate's `@context` is RO-Crate 1.3's, then `{"qro": "https://github.com/loganw234/QRO-Crate/blob/main/docs/VOCABULARY.md#"}`, and nothing else. A term's meaning never changes under its name; a changed meaning is a new term.

## What the shapes cannot see

1. **The checker is the authority.** A shape is a consequence of what the checker holds. Tests hold two things, and the second is narrower. When a must shape fails, the checker refuses the crate (steps 1 to 3): over every plant, a seeded fuzz and every one of the 12,591 single edits of the fixture that the first verifier's pool makes. When a crate is one fault away from one the checker accepts, it is refused by a name that a failing shape claims: over the same edits, 124 crates with a key spelt another way, and 469 crates of three families the second verifier found and the pool never made (an @id added again with a term of its own, or a path the reader holds as another's; a top-level @context or key of the crate's own; a File added whose file the disk lacks, or a link). Every must shape claims, beside the refusals it mirrors, the six of steps 1 and 2 that can come before its own and that RDF cannot show: `spelling`, `term-unknown`, `graph-form`, `context`, `file-missing` and `file-link`. Each is seen needed: with it left out, the sweeps find a crate on which a must shape fails and the checker's refusal is claimed by no failing shape (`context` through a real engine, which reads the crate's own context where the evaluator abstains; `file-link`, claimed from reading the checker's walk, by a File added at the path of a link, which is a junction on Windows, where no privilege is needed, and a symbolic link elsewhere). A crate with several faults is refused too, but its first refusal can be a fault no failing shape mirrors, and then its name is not claimed. A crate the expansion cannot read, one with an id the reader refuses or a context of its own, is never left out of these: the evaluator abstains from it, the checker has refused it, and the engine stage reads the contexts through a real engine. A walk over every crate plant of any parcel whose control row says it is accepted is written; none is built yet (the one accepted is a custody log), so it has examined no crate. These are samples, not proofs; limit 19 says what is held of ids, and at which base. What the shapes do not say is the checker's alone.
2. **The shapes are held to one engine, and to an evaluator of this repository's.** A real engine, pyshacl 0.40.1 on rdflib 7.6.0, reads the Turtle in the engine stage, which runs only where one is named (QRO_SHACL_PYTHON), and the quick budget's gates read the same shapes as data with an in-process evaluator. A construct the micro cases and the per-crate comparison do not hold is held by neither, and another engine may read a construct differently (limit 23 names three things on which the evaluator and pyshacl differ). Regular expressions are Python's `re` in both; they are written in the syntax an XPath engine shares, and no other engine was run. The shapes are for an engine run without inference: pyshacl's `inference` is `none`, its default, in the engine stage and wherever these shapes are used. With `rdfs`, `owlrl` or `both` it fails the accepted fixture crate on `descriptor`, `entity` and `profile-entities`, with 94, 112 and 527 results, because the shapes judge the graph a crate says and an inference adds triples to it: types that their lists of types do not allow (`rdfs:Resource` and `rdf:Property`; with OWL-RL `owl:Thing`, `rdfs:Datatype` and others) and self-triples that their closed shapes do not allow (`rdfs:subPropertyOf`; with OWL-RL `owl:sameAs`, `rdfs:subClassOf` and others). MEASURED: the counts by P4's fourth verifier and again by the engine stage, which holds them; the types and self-triples by one run of P4's fifth-round builder over the results' paths and values, which no test holds.
3. **Some spellings are looser in a shape than in the checker.** A size above 2^63 - 1 or with a trailing line feed; a rational not in lowest terms, with a term of more than 1,000 digits, or with a trailing line feed; a binary64 whose decimal is not the bits' exact one, or with a trailing line feed; a time that is not real (30 February, :60, T24:00) or with a trailing line feed; a date that is not real (month 13, 30 February); an iri with a trailing line feed; a text with a control character, a lone surrogate or a trailing line feed. A pattern holds a form, not that a date is real, a fraction reduced or a decimal exact. The trailing line feed is Python's `re`, where `$` matches before a final line feed; a SPARQL engine may not allow it (BELIEVED, not re-read).
4. **A `local-file` is read as any `File`, and the digest rule is for `file:` IRIs.** `domain-sha256` and `domain-contentsize` admit any File, and `file-digest-present` asks a digest of a File whose IRI is a `file:` IRI with no `#`, which is what a relative id resolves to against the evaluator's base. A File with another absolute IRI (`https:`, `urn:`) is exempt, as the checker exempts it, and read from a base that is not `file:`, no File is judged. A File whose id is itself an absolute `file:` IRI would be asked a digest by a real engine, which reads it as a path in the crate, and the checker asks none (MEASURED, the plant `abstains-absolute-file-id`). The reader refuses such an id `spelling` (FORMAT.md item 22), so no accepted crate has one, and the evaluator abstains from the crate (limit 19). A remote File, an absolute IRI that is no path in the crate, carrying a sha256 is refused `graph-form` by the checker, whether or not the root lists it, since sha256 stands only on a File the crate holds; the shapes read it as any File, so it conforms where the root lists it in `hasPart`, and fails `file-reached` where the root does not, a shape that claims `graph-form` (MEASURED, listed and unlisted, with and without a contentSize).
5. **A key no context defines never reaches RDF.** JSON-LD drops it, so a crate with `madeUp` conforms to the shapes and is refused `term-unknown`. A key RO-Crate's context spells another way (`schema:name` or the absolute IRI, for `name`) reaches RDF as the table's own term. The checker refuses it `term-unknown` (`graph-form` on the descriptor and on a contextual Profile entity, whose keys it holds one by one), whatever the shapes say: they may conform (a valid value, on an entity that has none) or fail (a second `name`, a value in no spelling, a term where its domain does not admit it), and when they fail a failing shape claims the refusal (every must shape claims `term-unknown`). A type spelt another way (`MediaObject` for `File`, `schema:Dataset`) is the same.
6. **One value and a one-element list, the order of a list, of the graph and of a type list are invisible to RDF.** A `name` written as a list of one, and a `hasPart` out of order, conform to the shapes and are refused `spelling`. An empty list makes no triple: `license: []` fails the root's shape for a missing license, and the checker refuses the form, `spelling`, which every must shape claims.
7. **Bytes, files, counts and every re-derivation are the checker's alone.** A moved shot, a digest that is not its file's, a stated count one too high and an adjusted count conform to every shape and are refused `raw-digest`, `file-digest`, `count-unpaid` and `raw-form`. So is everything steps 4 to 9 re-derive.
8. **`should/` holds rule 2's absence shapes, and `may/` is empty.** Nothing in the format is an optional behaviour a shape can state. Recommended practice is checked only by rule 2's absence rule, as a Warning.
9. **The Profile Crate is held by this repository's own check, not by RO-Crate's validator.** `check_profile_crate` holds the MUSTs of RO-Crate 1.3's profiles page that bytes show (the root typed Dataset and Profile, the human-readable description a File about the root that `hasPart` lists, a contextual Profile entity for every profile the root is a profile of, and for an entity that conforms to JSON-LD's Context an absolute `@id` and the encodingFormat `application/ld+json`), the SHOULDs its docstring lists (the root's absolute `@id`, name, `isProfileOf` and `hasPart`; for each resource a role, an artifact, and on each artifact an `encodingFormat`) and the core's. It holds no more: limits 11, 17 and 22 state the SHOULDs not met. Its root `@id` is an absolute IRI, as RO-Crate's examples have it; rocrate-validator's rule that a root data entity's URI end with a slash may refuse that (BELIEVED, not run).
10. **rocrate-validator 0.12.2 was not run on these shapes, and cannot check Process Run Crate 0.6.** Its Process Run Crate profile is 0.5, and the types its ontology infers may trip the closed shape. Its folder layout is followed as read, not as run.
11. **The profile's IRIs are provisional.** The profile IRI is this page, and no machine-readable Profile Crate is served from it; GitHub lowercases a page's anchors, so a camelCase term's fragment lands on its row only by luck. A tool that follows RO-Crate's retrieval order finds no Profile Crate from the IRI. The entity that represents the JSON-LD context has, as the absolute `@id` RO-Crate 1.3 asks, the raw GitHub URL of context.jsonld on main. RO-Crate asks it to be retrievable as JSON-LD, a permalink and versioned: this one moves with the branch, and the host is believed to serve the file as `text/plain` (BELIEVED, not fetched). The profile's `identifier` is not set, since it is for a permanent IRI. At the switch to a permanent IRI the entity is regenerated with the rest.
12. **A crate under a provisional IRI is a different crate from the same crate under a permanent one.** The identity digest covers both IRIs, and a custody log names digests, so no crate is to be published or archived under a provisional IRI, and at the switch every generated file and every crate is regenerated, never edited.
13. **One version at a time.** The checker, the reader and these shapes read this version. A crate declaring another is refused `context`; reading two would need two tables chosen by the declared version.
14. **The fixture needs `--fixtures`.** P0's fixture has its own raw form and generator, which only the checker's `--fixtures` registers, so the plain command line refuses the example `step-unbuilt`, by design.
15. **The matrix lists only this profile's own plants.** Another parcel's crate plants are held to the shapes' soundness, and are not described here.
16. **Presence rules are this profile's own, until the table says where a term is required.** A presence rule a later step adds is not a must shape until someone writes the line: the shapes are then weaker than the checker, never stricter.
17. **The levels of the study's section 9 are not expressed by any shape.** Recorded, anchored, comparable and quantum-comparable are properties of a comparison, not of a crate's graph. The description file's media type is `text/markdown`, where RO-Crate asks `text/html`.
18. **A report's `sh:conforms` is false for a Warning or an Info too.** That is the Recommendation. A user who runs an engine on a crate with only should-level results sees "does not conform" and filters by severity.
19. **An id is read at one base, as FORMAT.md item 22 admits it, and item 22's own limits pass to the shapes.** The reader admits an @id, and a reference's, in four forms only: the root, a path in the crate, a fragment, and an absolute IRI whose scheme is lowercase and neither `file` nor a prefix of the context. For every id it accepts the expansion makes the IRI rdflib 7.6.0 makes, at the base `file:///crate/`, and distinct ids are distinct IRIs: held by the engine stage over tens of thousands of ids drawn from the four forms and from every short string of the characters that bite, and by the quick stage's gates on the expansion's side. The ids the reader refuses and a JSON-LD reader reads otherwise (`_:b0` as a blank node, `@x` as the root, `a//b` as `a/b`, `//x` as another host, a `file:` IRI as a path) the expansion refuses to read where it knows rdflib's reading, and the evaluator then abstains. That is harmless, since the checker has refused the crate and no gate skips one. A real engine reads such a crate its own way and may fail a shape the evaluator never sees (`entity` on `_:b0`, `term-name` on `@x`, `file-digest-present` on an absolute `file:` id, `term-haspart` on a reference to `_:b0`: the plants of the family `abstains`, MEASURED, pyshacl 0.40.1), on a crate the checker refused first, by a name the failing shape claims: the checker refuses an id outside the rule `spelling`, and a reference outside it `graph-form`, and every must shape claims both. What stays is item 22's own, and it binds the shapes. A crate read where it lives is read at another base, and an absolute IRI equal to the IRI a relative id resolves to is one node with it (`https://example.org/crate/x` beside the path `x`, read at `https://example.org/crate/`): a term shape can then fail on two entities the checker holds apart, and at `file:///crate/` no such IRI is an id. An absolute IRI and a fragment are held to their characters, not to the rest of RFC 3986's grammar (`http://a:b:c/`), which a processor that converts only well-formed IRIs drops. rdflib departs from JSON-LD 1.1 at a base urllib does not join (`mailto:`, `s3:`, `data:`) and at one with an empty path. A JSON-LD 1.0 processor makes a prefix of every term of the context, and RO-Crate 1.3 names no version, so to such a processor an absolute IRI whose scheme is a term (`geo:x`, `name:x`) is another IRI (BELIEVED, from 1.0's rule; none was run).
20. **A graph with no descriptor or no root has nothing for those shapes to judge.** The descriptor and root shapes have the descriptor and what it is about for focus nodes; the checker refuses a crate without them `graph-form`.
21. **A name RO-Crate's context gives a listed type passes the type check.** `MediaObject` is `File` in RDF, so a type written `MediaObject` conforms and is refused `term-unknown`.
22. **The extension terms are mapped by one prefix, not each by its code.** RO-Crate 1.3 asks the `termCode` of a DefinedTerm to be valid as a key in a conforming crate's context, and the term to be mapped to its `@id` in the Profile Crate's `@context`. The Profile Crate's `@context` maps the one prefix a QRO crate's maps, `qro`, so that every `qro:code` is its DefinedTerm's `@id`. The codes are not mapped as bare keys: QRO crates write `qro:code`, and some codes (`device`, `line`, `value` and `Question` today) are terms of RO-Crate's own context, which a mapping in the Profile Crate would redefine. That SHOULD is not met.
23. **The evaluator and pyshacl read three things differently, and none changes a verdict on a crate.** `sh:minLength 0` on a blank node: the evaluator fails it, since a blank node has no string to measure (READ, the Recommendation's section 4.4.1, in an extraction), and pyshacl 0.40.1 does not. `sh:maxInclusive` with no `sh:minInclusive`, against a boolean literal: the evaluator fails it, since a boolean has no order with a number, and pyshacl 0.40.1 passes it (BELIEVED the evaluator is right, from SPARQL's comparison rules; not re-read). MEASURED by 28,000 random shapes over random graphs, through the engine stage's runner (P4's second verifier): these were the only disagreements, in 16 cases and 2. The generated shapes use neither: no `sh:minLength` is below 1 (`sh:maxLength` is used, with several bounds, and the two read it alike), and no `sh:maxInclusive` stands without its `sh:minInclusive`; a test holds that, and the engine stage holds the two disagreements as they are, so that a new engine is noticed. A shape written with either would be read two ways, and its micro case would have to say which. The third is the lexical form of an integer. The generated shapes do use `sh:datatype xsd:integer` (three terms), and on a literal whose lexical form Python's `int()` reads and XSD's lexical space may not (`' 1'`, `'1 '`, a tab and a line feed around `1`, `'1_0'`, U+0661 and U+FF11, and others of their kinds: other white space, an underscore between digits, the digits of other scripts) the evaluator fails the shape, as for an ill-formed literal, and pyshacl accepts the literal, because rdflib 7.6.0 maps an integer's lexical form with Python's `int()` and calls a literal well formed when it has a value (READ, rdflib/term.py in the pinned environment; MEASURED by P4's fourth verifier and again in the engine stage, which holds the six forms as they are and their neighbours, where the two agree). No crate reaches these forms. The reader takes an integer only as a JSON number in its one spelling and refuses any other `spelling`, and the expansion writes a number as its decimal digits alone (held in the quick stage), so the soundness of the shapes is untouched. What the tree can say of which judge is right: the checker refuses all six forms, so pyshacl's reading is the looser, which is the safe direction and no claim of more than the checker holds, and the evaluator's agrees with the checker's. What it cannot say: which is right by XSD 1.1 and RDF 1.1 Concepts, since it pins no copy of either. BELIEVED, from XSD 1.1's definition of the integer, recalled and not re-read: its lexical space is an optional sign and ASCII digits, so the evaluator is right on `'1_0'` and on the two digits; on the three forms with white space it turns on whether XSD's collapse of white space applies to an RDF literal's lexical form, which is not settled here.

## The examples

[EXAMPLES.md](EXAMPLES.md) lists every positive example and every plant and what each layer says of it. P0's fixture, in [examples/fixture/](examples/fixture/), is accepted by `python -m qro check --fixtures`; without `--fixtures` the checker refuses it `step-unbuilt`, since its raw form and generator are the fixture's.
